title: Redis connection checks can leak broker credentials into logs
reasoning: check_redis_connectivity logs the full broker_url on both success and failure. REDIS_URL commonly embeds usernames or passwords, especially for hosted Redis providers, and bahk.settings sources Celery broker URLs directly from REDIS_URL. Logging the full URL can expose Redis credentials to application logs and Sentry breadcrumbs/events.
reproduction: Set REDIS_URL to a credential-bearing URL such as redis://:password@example:6379/0 and start a Celery worker; the connectivity log includes app.conf.broker_url.
recommendation: Sanitize broker URLs before logging or sending exception context, preserving only scheme, host, port, and database index. Avoid capturing full connection strings in Sentry context.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise Celery worker startup signals or assert log redaction behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for check_redis_connectivity logging with a password-bearing broker URL and assert the password is not present in emitted log records.
minimumFixScope: Introduce a small URL redaction helper in bahk/celery.py and use it for Redis connectivity logs.
